StringWithMarkup.String: Barium stimulates striated, cardiac, and smooth muscle, regardless of innervation. It is antagonistic to all muscle depressants, no matter whether they act primarily on nerve or muscle. Initial stimulation of contraction leads to vasoconstriction through direct action on arterial muscle, peristalsis through action on smooth muscle, tremors and cramps through action on the skeletal muscles, and various arrhythmias through action on the heart. If the dose is sufficient, stimulation is followed by weakness and eventually by paralysis of the different kinds of muscle. Some effects such as hypertension, violent tremors, and convulsions are uncommon following ingestion of barium carbonate. They are more likely to follow absorption of more soluble barium compounds. If death does occur, it is caused by failure of muscular contraction leading to respiratory failure or cardiovascular collapse.

Section.Description: The threshold limit value (TLV) of a chemical is an airborne concentration at which a worker can be exposed day after day for a working lifetime without adverse effect. [2] Threshold limit value - short-term exposure limit (TLV-STEL): a 15-minute TWA exposure that should not be exceeded at any time during a workday, even if the 8-hour TWA is within the TLV-TWA. [3] Threshold limit value - ceiling limit (TLV-C): absolute exposure limit that should not be exceeded at any time.
